FINDINGS. Both share ONE root cause (R1): the subsystem has no single core-owned authority for "which language identities are already held for this choice". The satisfaction predicate (characterDraft.ts:828-837, 1693-1714) computes held = fixed grants (incl. custom background) UNION languages claimed by earlier satisfied language groups, under languageKey. Every option-producing and CLI boundary recomputes a narrower notion: requiredChoices.ts:592-599 uses exact strings over fixed grants only; characterWizard.ts:1131/1190 use exact strings over the current group only; characterWizard.ts:1166-1168 re-implements languageKey inline over the current group only. Prior repairs patched predicates one by one; the menus and CLI never got the same identity OR the same scope. S1 is the identity facet, S2 the scope facet.

S1 - BLOCKING (identity facet; Sol 19.3.3.6 S1, unchanged at this head). RECOMMENDED SINGLE ARCHITECTURAL CLOSURE (one repair closes R1): 
(1) Core computes held-language identities ONCE, in characterDraft's mechanicalChoices, in the same ordered pass as isLanguageChoiceSatisfied (fixed grants incl. custom background, then each language group's claims), and uses that one result both to subtract from each language choice's from (replacing requiredChoices' private exact-string chooseableLanguages, or passing it the held keys) and to judge satisfaction. Expose the held list on each language choice state (e.g. MechanicalChoiceState.heldLanguages, canonical spellings) and an unsatisfied-reason (collision with X) so the CLI can be actionable.
(2) languageKey is the only identity function: promote it (or an isSameLanguage predicate) to the @eshyra/core root export, since the CLI is a production caller and may import only the root; delete the CLI's inline identity at 1166-1168 and use it at 1131, 1166-1168 and 1190, checking against selected UNION heldLanguages.
(3) Optional but recommended: canonicalize language spellings at the core write/load boundary (setChoice for language ids, setGmApprovedLanguages, setBackgroundCustomization.languages, draft load) with canonicalLanguageName, known = pack fixed grants, defaults and the table:standard-languages / table:exotic-languages languageOptions projections (reachable via the extension refs). Decide the in-domain-variant admission policy once (rows 9/13) and keep it consistent.
Preserve: Standard default domains, explicit approval admission/clearing, quantities, sheet string-array shape; never dedupe an accepted invalid grant after the fact.
Permanent evidence (proportionate, generalized, not per-spelling reproducers): ONE property invariant "offered implies acceptable and held implies not offered" over every bundled language-choice producer (Human, Half-Elf, High Elf x ordinary Acolyte and custom Acolyte) with canonical and case/whitespace-variant held inputs and a prior-group claim; plus ONE CLI test covering a cross-group duplicate refusal (with reason, no mutation) and a resumed variant-spelling input, then a distinct pick completing the group.

NOT FINDINGS (no requirement): exact default-domain membership (rows 9/13) - stricter, never widens. Approved exotic languages keep the GM-typed spelling on the sheet (no Exotic-table spelling in finalize known) - identity is unaffected and no consumer compares spelling. Raw backgroundCustomization.languages on the sheet - no consumer. Stale approvals after a single-pick replace - approval was explicit. Schema allows an extension on a fixed-only grant - no consumer. resolveOption prefix/substring in the other-language path - speculative. requiredChoices uses only the first language grant - pack has one grant per record. Additional per-spelling permanent tests or a new proof registry - no requirement.
